units.text: INT. LUMEN NAIL BAR - AFTERNOON

The salon smells of acetone and jasmine, and under that of something else, something nobody in the room has named yet; the dryers hum in a steady chord, the television above the pedicure chairs plays a cooking show on mute, and at the third station a woman in a grey hoodie sits with both hands flat on the table as though she were waiting for them to be read.
Any plans for the weekend, hon?
units.name: NORA

units.text: Not really. Maybe visit my sister. She lives out past the reservoir.
units.name: THE WOMAN
paren: voice flat, eyes on the window

units.text: Oh that's nice. Family is everything.
units.name: NORA

units.text: Is it.
units.name: THE WOMAN

units.text: Nora glances up.

Behind the counter, VIVIAN rings up a customer, tucking a stray lock behind her ear, and at the far chair THE TWINS, identical in matching pink smocks, murmur to each other in a rhythm too even to be conversation.
Do you smell it? Do you smell it?
units.name: THE TWINS

units.text: Girls, enough with the perfume jokes.
units.name: VIVIAN

units.text: Not perfume.
units.name: THE TWINS

units.text: They get like this when it rains. Ignore them.
units.name: NORA

units.text: It's not raining.
units.name: THE WOMAN

units.text: A silence.
The cooking show on the television flickers, goes to static, comes back.
In the corner, DEV the new tech, who has been sweeping the same square of floor for ten minutes, stops.
The wifi's dropped again. And the card reader. Everything just--
units.name: DEV

units.text: Dev. Floor.
units.name: VIVIAN

units.text: Sorry. Sorry.
units.name: DEV

units.text: So, what do you do, hon? For work?
units.name: NORA
paren: trying again, painting a clear coat

units.text: I count things. How many people, how many exits. How long the lights stay on.
units.name: THE WOMAN

units.text: That's a strange job.
units.name: NORA

units.text: It's a strange week.
units.name: THE WOMAN

units.text: The Twins stop murmuring.
Both rise from their chairs at the same instant, smocks rustling, and the room tilts toward them.
She is early.
units.name: THE TWINS

units.text: Who is early?
units.name: VIVIAN

units.text: Her. She was not supposed to come until Thursday.
units.name: THE TWINS

units.text: Hon, what are they talking about?
units.name: NORA

units.text: My name is Ilsa. And I am so sorry. I wanted one last manicure before the end.
units.name: THE WOMAN
paren: pushing back her hood to reveal pale, almost translucent skin

units.text: The end of what?
units.name: DEV

units.text: Of this. All of it. They said you'd want to know.
units.name: ILSA
paren: rising, her hands beginning to glow faintly under the dryer lamps

units.text: Nobody here asked.
units.name: VIVIAN

units.text: Nobody ever does.
units.name: ILSA

units.text: The television goes black.
Every dryer in the salon stops at once, and in the sudden quiet a single drop of polish falls from Nora's brush and rings against the tabletop like a bell.
